reason: The text demonstrates Yahweh actively intervening to preserve the wellbeing of the Hebrew people (בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל). When the Israelites face death from thirst in the wilderness, Moses appeals directly to Yahweh. Yahweh responds immediately with explicit instructions to strike the rock at Horeb to produce water for the people to drink. This miraculous provision directly addresses the life-threatening crisis, saving the people from perishing. The action itself—providing water when the people are desperate and dying—constitutes concrete evidence of Yahweh's care for their wellbeing.
